notes: The pool holds NO queue of its own: `judge()` is a per-decision call that immediately fans out one asyncio task per eligible route, and a task that cannot reserve a route slot returns `capacity` at once (judge_pool.py:430-431). 'Queue depth' here is therefore the caller-side outstanding-decision count, which is the only place work can pile up.

`max_parallel` is a PER-DECISION fan-out semaphore, constructed fresh inside every `judge()` call (judge_pool.py:568). It does not bound pool-wide concurrency. The only pool-wide bound is sum(JudgeCapability.max_inflight).

C_returned_object_aliasing.scenario: route A replies low-confidence before expiry; route B never replies; the pool concludes the decision by DEADLINE EXPIRY and hands back route A's object

notes: DEFECT (post-decision aliasing) — judge_pool.py:667 retains and judge_pool.py:695 returns the provider's own Verdict instance with no defensive copy, and percept/contracts/__init__.py:472 declares Verdict as a NON-frozen dataclass. A route whose reply was accepted (or merely retained as `uncertain`) can therefore rewrite satisfied/confidence after the pool has already concluded the decision and the caller has acted on it. Measured here: the pool concluded by deadline expiry and returned (False, 0.4); the provider then rewrote the same object to (True, 0.99). The ordinary decisive path is equally aliased (control: (False, 0.95) -> (True, 0.99)). SCOPE: this is an SDK-wide ownership convention, not something JudgePool introduces — the SDK's own FakeVision.judge (backends/fake.py:61-95) also hands back its scripted object by identity (control: aliased=True). It is nevertheless a real gap in the pool's 'a late provider reply cannot mutate a concluded decision' guarantee: only the synthesised-UNKNOWN paths (no_route / capacity / deadline with no retained reply) are actually immune. Fix would be a copy at judge_pool.py:659/667 or freezing Verdict.

The deadline is enforced by the outer `asyncio.wait(timeout=remaining)` loop (judge_pool.py:591-599) and the `finally` block that cancels every unfinished route task (judge_pool.py:696-716). Because `judge()` has already returned by then, a late reply is structurally unable to add a receipt or change the verdict — the only post-return state it touches is the route's inflight/failure counters.

audio_judge_binding.prepare_audio_judge_binding(JudgePool): ValueError: compiled audio requires an exact SDK-owned FakeVision or GeminiVision adapter

notes: ARCHITECTURE: `prepare_audio_judge_binding` (audio_input.py:1028-1062) accepts ONLY an exact SDK FakeVision or GeminiVision instance, so a JudgePool cannot be installed as a compiled AudioJudgeBinding. The compiled-audio dispatch therefore does NOT inherit the pool's capacity/deadline bounds — it is a frozen single-adapter dispatch. Pool parity on the `audio`/`fused` evidence shapes (proved above) applies when a JudgePool is used as the Vision adapter, not when the compiled-audio binding path is used.

`FakeSpecialist` (backends/fake.py:124) is a token streamer with no `judge()`, so it is not routable through JudgePool by construction (JudgeRoute.__post_init__, judge_pool.py:119-122). The specialist path exercised here is the `context_stream` evidence shape — the context-holding route the module docstring calls out at line 10-11.
